scope: The five-option workbench passes as a bounded decision surface. No individual presentation is human-approved or production authority.

hierarchy.reason: Each option declares a different first read, and the recommended social-caption variant gives account evidence, quote and portrait an unambiguous sequence.

composition.reason: Items are 1000 to 1160px wide and 309 to 336px high at 1440. The track has no chassis, fill or card outline; the compact receiver-width correction prevents clipped copy.

pacing.reason: The slow 24px/s drift, broad line lengths and 48px controls create measured proof pacing. Five stacked demo rails are appropriate only in the workbench comparison, not a production page.

typography.reason: Display, quote, account and technical roles remain disciplined. Real long quotes are readable without introducing card-title ornament.

productTruth.reason: Seven real clips, quotes, profiles and follower snapshots replace placeholders, and Daniel is honestly absent. Five follower counts were publicly checked; two retain source-project attribution and therefore stay a known gap.

distinctiveness.reason: Live halftone people, a restrained Instagram evidence line and an open editorial rail remain recognisably Mez after colour and motion are stripped away.

narrative.reason: The workbench moves from five hierarchy choices to measured motion truth and ends at the open human decision.

conversionClarity.reason: CMP-06 has no conversion CTA by design; Pause, Previous, Next and Instagram are clearly named and visually distinct.

emotionalResonance.reason: Moving real faces and first-person operator language create warmth without testimonial theatre or fabricated identity marks.

craft.reason: A fractional motion accumulator, clean seam, passive direct input, explicit pause states, hidden clone semantics and complete reduced-motion list are resolved together.

originality.reason: The five options vary composition rather than decorative skins and avoid the familiar glossy testimonial-card carousel.

T1StripTest.method: All five 1440px renders were inspected in their neutral palette and without relying on portrait animation.
T1StripTest.evidence: Hierarchy survives through proportion, source line, type and one structural rule. No gradient, glow, texture or ornamental colour is needed.

T2ComponentRepetitionTest.method: The five adjacent desktop variants and compact convergence were inspected as one comparison surface.
T2ComponentRepetitionTest.evidence: Profile strip, portrait window, social caption, quote first and proof ledger change reading order and spatial logic. They are not five skins on one card.

T3MotionComparisonTest.method: Track scrollLeft was sampled for 1,500ms while running and 1,200ms after Pause. A visible 160 by 160 halftone crop was compared 1,250ms apart at an 8-level RGB threshold in the in-app Browser.
T3MotionComparisonTest.evidence: The rail advanced 36px at the contracted 24px/s and moved 0px while paused. The portrait changed in 7,002 of 25,600 pixels, or 27.35%. Offscreen workbench components had 0 live portraits and 0 playing videos.

T4RealContentTest.method: All renders used the seven-record AI OS fixture, local prepared portrait clips and supplied Instagram evidence.
T4RealContentTest.evidence: Seven primary items and seven aria-hidden loop items rendered in moving mode; Daniel was absent; real long and short quotes remained coherent.

canonScan.notes: No mesh gradient, indigo-violet palette, glass, ambient shadow, backdrop blur, generic card grid or decorative filler appears. Continuous carousel drift conflicts with DEC-WEBSITE-MOTION-SYSTEM-001 and is carried only by Olli's recorded CMP-06 bounded exception.

findings.finding: Sub-pixel scrollLeft assignments rounded away and could report running without visible motion.
findings.resolution: Added a fractional autoOffset accumulator; measured movement is now exactly 36px in 1.5 seconds.

findings.finding: At 320px the item exceeded the receiver by 14px and clipped the final words while paused.
findings.resolution: Item width now uses receiver container units and matches the 280px host.

findings.finding: Social caption best balances platform familiarity and Mez ownership; proof ledger is the strongest more-editorial alternative.
findings.resolution: Leave both and the three requested contrasts visible for Olli's decision; do not promote one silently.

humanGate.question: Which Round 02 presentation, if any, should move forward: profile strip, portrait window, social caption, quote first or proof ledger?
